# GitHub Workflow Requirements Quality Checklist: Document branch naming and lifecycle

**Purpose**: Review the requirements quality of the branch lifecycle and contributor workflow guidance for clarity, completeness, traceability, and repository governance alignment.
**Created**: 2026-09-20
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the lifecycle rules for `spec/*`, `feature/*`, and `impl/*` clearly and completely documented for contributors? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003]
- [x] CHK002 Are the merge and review requirements stated in a way that covers the full protected-branch workflow? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, §FR-005]
- [x] CHK003 Are the repository references for the PR template and branch protection guidance explicitly included in the requirements? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK004 Are the expected branch cleanup conditions documented when auto-delete-on-merge is enabled? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK005 Is the difference between specification-work branches and implementation-work branches described with specific, unambiguous guidance? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003]
- [x] CHK006 Is the term "pull request" defined in the context of repository governance so contributors understand when it is mandatory? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK007 Is the approval requirement quantified clearly enough to avoid ambiguity about review expectations? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK008 Is the documentation written in plain language without introducing implementation-specific or hidden workflow assumptions? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK009 Do the branch naming conventions align with the repository constitution and the issue-driven workflow? [Consistency, Constitution §4, Spec §FR-002, §FR-003]
- [x] CHK010 Do the merge and approval requirements align with the PR policy and protected-branch governance in the constitution? [Consistency, Constitution §5, Spec §FR-004, §FR-005]
- [x] CHK011 Is the documentation consistent with the existing repository workflow and metadata, including the PR template stage fields? [Consistency, Plan §Summary, Spec §FR-007]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK012 Are the success criteria measurable enough to confirm that contributors can identify the correct branch lifecycle and merge flow without confusion? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-003]
- [x] CHK013 Can the expected documentation outcome be objectively verified from the contributor guidance alone? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001, §SC-004]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK014 Are the main contributor scenarios covered for initial branch creation, implementation work, PR creation, and merge review? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1, §User Story 2, §User Story 3]
- [x] CHK015 Are the key exception scenarios identified, including uncertainty about branch type selection and the risk of bypassing the PR process? [Coverage, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK016 Are recovery and corrective scenarios addressed, such as contributors needing to re-check the repo workflow after an incorrect branch decision? [Coverage, Gap, Edge Cases]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK017 Are the repository assumptions about protected branches, PR usage, and authoritative workflow references clearly identified and consistent with the project governance? [Assumption, Constitution §4, §5]
- [x] CHK018 Are dependencies on GitHub repository settings and the PR template documented as configuration references rather than hidden requirements? [Dependency, Spec §FR-007]

## Traceability & Review Readiness

- [x] CHK019 Can the final documentation be traced back to the originating GitHub issue and the feature specification without ambiguity? [Traceability, Issue #24, Spec §Input]
- [x] CHK020 Are all workflow requirements aligned with the issue’s requested guidance and the repository’s branch-protection expectations? [Traceability, Spec §FR-001, §FR-007]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
